name: analog-lead-into-braam
idea: The lead performer is a sad-heroic monophonic analog synth lead (chorus-wide saw, a little portamento) over a pulsing 16th-note analog bass, Juno-style detuned pads and a LinnDrum beat with a gated-reverb snare, at 120 BPM, for the first four seconds only. At about 4 s the drums and lead cut out on one huge low synth-horn braam, and the same 120 BPM pulse carries on as a dry, ticking low-string and sub ostinato with metallic hits, one per beat, so every half-second cut gets a hit. The hits darken and thicken to about 17 s, then the whole track drops in pitch and speed like a tape stop and is silent from about 20 s. Ask for it by period and gear in short tags (1980s film-score synths, 2010s revival, analog, drum machine), tempo first; exclude EDM drop, trap, autotune, big pop chorus, vocals, choir.

name: aero-glass-bells
idea: The lead is a glassy FM electric piano and crystal bell synth playing bright major-seventh chords, with airy reverb, soft bubbly digital blips and a relaxed mid-tempo 2000s chillout beat around 95 BPM, the clean optimistic sound of mid-2000s computer start-up music rather than straight synthwave. At about 4 s the bells are frozen into a long reverb tail and a falling Shepard-tone drone takes over, with deep sub rumbles and distant processed impacts instead of a beat, so the dread is sound design, not orchestra. The drone keeps sinking and thinning from about 17 s until there is nothing left by 20 s. Ask for it as a mood and texture description (glossy, airy, nostalgic tech optimism, then cold ambient horror drone) rather than gear names; exclude drums after the turn, EDM drop, trap, vocals, choir, big pop chorus.

name: slowed-sax-meme-edit
idea: The lead is a smooth, breathy late-80s-style synth saxophone melody over warm slap-free fretless bass, glossy pads and a soft drum machine at about 100 BPM, already slightly slowed and drenched in reverb like a 2016 meme edit of old mall music: happy, hazy, a little too nostalgic. At about 4 s the saxophone and beat drop out mid-phrase and are replaced by detuned, warped tape-wobbled pads under an anxious ticking clock and low distorted bass pulses, as if the same cassette had gone bad. The warble gets heavier and darker to about 17 s, then everything slows and sags in pitch to a standstill and silence by about 20 s. Ask for it through the slowed-and-reverb, VHS-tape, chopped meme-edit production words plus the two moods; exclude vocals, choir, trap hi-hats, EDM drop, autotune, big pop chorus.

name: piano-to-orchestra-trailer
idea: The lead is a solo grand piano playing a simple, hopeful major-key melody on top of a light synthwave arpeggio and a soft analog pad at 120 BPM, a warm cinematic opening for the first four seconds. At about 4 s the piano stops on one dissonant low cluster and a full hybrid trailer orchestra comes in: driving staccato low strings on every beat, deep taiko and orchestral percussion hits, brass swells and a rising riser that climbs through the reel, so the half-second cuts ride the beat. Around 17 s the orchestra slows down like a ritardando into a held low string note that fades to complete silence by about 20 s, with no final hit. Ask for it as a short cinematic trailer cue described section by section with rough timings in the style box (warm intro, hard turn, building dread, slowing to silence); exclude vocals, choir, EDM drop, dubstep, trap, autotune, pop chorus.
